principles: Original semantic construction for AI Council signature concepts; familiar controls preserve convention.
Static semantic recognition outranks clever geometry.
Monochrome geometry first; semantic color belongs to the Visual System state.
Nodes, lines, cuts, and relationships appear only when they carry meaning.
Icon absence is part of the system: having a glyph available does not imply displaying it.
No icon world may remove or simplify away a difficult calibration concept to look cleaner.
The selected world must survive 14–18px use and dense repetition before the family can scale.
The first independent review may rank or reject worlds but may not recommend hybridization.

worlds.label: Quiver Construct
worlds.origin: Evolves the Visual System's Quiver Line hypothesis but has no selection authority.
worlds.idea: Quiet directional tension: open constructions, precise cuts, and controlled vector convergence communicate decisions and movement without becoming arrow decoration.
worlds.signatureBehavior: A limited 45°/90° directional family and open terminals create forward intent; nodes appear only at real registrations or convergence points.

hybridInheritance.threshold: harder cuts only for authority/consequence semantics

geometry.nodeRule: 3px or smaller registration nodes only when semantic

worlds.risk: Can drift into developer-tool arrows, miniature flowcharts, or repeated directional motifs if every concept receives a quiver treatment.

worlds.label: Editorial Sign
worlds.origin: Counterpoint-dominant challenger focused on human recognition and quiet symbolic form.
worlds.idea: Reduced, human-facing signs use optical asymmetry and calm silhouette to make AI Council feel considered rather than machine-obsessed.
worlds.signatureBehavior: Fewer strokes, selectively curved constructions, and asymmetric optical balance create readable signs; technology is implied by precision, not by nodes or networks.

hybridInheritance.decisionSpine: relationships appear only in signature semantics that require lineage
hybridInheritance.counterpoint: primary owner of proportion, quietness, and human judgment
hybridInheritance.threshold: authority glyph may become more rigid without changing the whole family

geometry.nodeRule: avoid nodes unless they are the only clean way to express registration

worlds.risk: Can become beautiful but generic editorial signage and lose enough structural specificity that provenance, supersession, or authority semantics blur together.

worlds.label: Provenance Glyph
worlds.origin: AI-Council-specific challenger derived from lineage, registration, state replacement, and durable project truth.
worlds.idea: Small structural marks encode registration, continuity, replacement, and boundary semantics so the family feels native to evidence-backed decisions and durable project memory.
worlds.signatureBehavior: Interrupted lines, restrained registration nodes, open frames, and state handoffs reveal just enough relationship to make provenance and supersession distinctive without becoming a network diagram.

hybridInheritance.decisionSpine: primary owner of relationship and state transformation grammar
hybridInheritance.counterpoint: forces simplification and quiet optical weight
hybridInheritance.threshold: boundary semantics become explicit only for authority/risk concepts

geometry.nodeRule: small circular or diamond registration only at semantically meaningful state junctions

worlds.risk: Can become self-referential technical glyphs or tiny topology diagrams, especially below 18px, if relationship grammar is used where simple recognition would be better.
